name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Electromagnetic Javelin EJ-4 'Thunderbolt'
description:
A 180-centimeter javelin with an electromagnetic acceleration system in the grip that can be used in two modes: as a conventional thrusting spear with vibro-enhanced tip, or as a self-propelled projectile that the operator throws and the electromagnetic system accelerates to three times natural throwing speed. The Thunderbolt bridges the gap between melee weapon and ranged armament.

In spear mode, the EJ-4 functions as a vibrating thrusting weapon with a carbon-lattice shaft and an Ablonite-KR ceramic tip that penetrates armor through a combination of vibration-assisted micro-fracturing and sheer material hardness. The weapon is balanced for single-handed use with a shield or paired with a shorter sidearm.

In javelin mode, the operator activates the electromagnetic acceleration as they throw, and the grip-mounted linear accelerator adds approximately 40 meters per second to the throwing velocity. The accelerated javelin penetrates light vehicle armor at 30 meters and defeats personal armor at 50 meters. The electromagnetic system is single-use per throw — the weapon must be retrieved and the capacitor recharged before it can accelerate again. This disposable-use throwing mode transforms the Thunderbolt from a defensive spear into an offensive anti-armor weapon that can be deployed with no setup time.
specifications:
total_length: 180 cm
weight: 1.5 kg
shaft_material: Carbon-lattice composite
tip_material: Ablonite-KR ceramic with vibro system
tip_vibration: 38,000 Hz
throw_acceleration: +40 m/s over natural throwing velocity
effective_throw_range: 50 meters against personnel, 30 meters against vehicles
power_source: Grip capacitor, 1 accelerated throw per charge, 3 hours vibro mode
tactical_use: The Thunderbolt provides operators with a melee weapon that doubles as a single-shot ranged anti-armor system. In defensive positions, it functions as a reach-advantage spear with vibro-enhanced penetration. When an opportunity presents — an armored vehicle approaching, a high-value target in the open, a critical system that must be disabled from range — the operator throws the Thunderbolt with electromagnetic acceleration, delivering armor-defeating kinetic energy at distances no other thrown weapon can match. The one-shot limitation means the throw must be decisive; missed throws leave the operator without their primary weapon.
cultural_context: The electromagnetic javelin has captured imaginations in GLMZ's combat culture in a way that more sophisticated weapons have not. There is something primal about a thrown spear — and a thrown spear that pierces vehicle armor speaks to a deep human satisfaction in simple solutions to complex problems. Thunderbolt throwing competitions have emerged as a spectator sport, with operators competing for distance, accuracy, and most impressively, penetration through standardized armor targets. The sport has attracted corporate sponsorship, which some participants view as ironic given that the weapon was designed to fight corporate security.
story_hooks: A Thunderbolt was thrown through an armored corporate transport's engine compartment from a rooftop 45 meters away — a shot that exceeded the weapon's rated penetration by a factor of two. Either the weapon was modified or the operator is superhumanly strong. Arcturus wants to know which.

A javelin competition has been infiltrated by an operator who is using the events as cover to scout security arrangements at the venue — a corporate headquarters that hosts the competitions on its grounds. The next throw might not be aimed at a target.

physical_description.visual_profile: An elongated javelin with a pronounced grip section roughly one-third down from the top. The weapon presents as a sleek fusion of melee and ranged design — the upper two-thirds taper to a needle-sharp ceramic point, while the lower section features a noticeably thickened grip housing containing visible electromagnetic coils and a subtle grid of heat-dissipation vents. The overall impression is 'precision instrument,' not brute force.
physical_description.dimensions: 180 cm total length; tip to grip transition at approximately 120 cm; grip assembly 15 cm long × 6 cm wide
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably balanced and light for its length — 1.5 kg feels almost buoyant in hand due to carbon-lattice construction. The weight concentrates in the grip section (housing the capacitor), making it neither top-heavy nor awkward. Single-handed grip feels natural; negligible fatigue during extended hold.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-lattice composite shaft (80% of structure); Ablonite-KR ceramic reinforced tip; grip assembly combines lightweight alloy frame with polymer composite skin
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on the shaft with a subtle satin sheen; grip section features brushed nickel plating on exposed coil housings; the ceramic tip has a polished, almost glass-like translucent white finish with faint internal fracture patterns visible under light (indicating the material's micro-lattice structure)
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray shaft, brushed silver grip assembly, pearl-white ceramic tip. Subtle teal accent striping along the grip's electromagnetic coil housing indicates active power status.
physical_description.grip_texture: Soft-touch rubberized polymer with embedded conductive threading for feedback; faint grid pattern molded into palm contact area for secure control even with wet or augmented hands. The grip feels warm to the touch from the capacitor beneath.
distinctive_features: Three small teal LED indicator lights arranged vertically on the grip — top (capacitor charge status), middle (vibro system active), bottom (throw-lock safety)
Linear accelerator coil housing visible as raised ribs along grip sides, giving a distinctive ribbed silhouette
Heat-dissipation micro-vents (pin-sized) scattered across grip in organic pattern
Slight iridescence in the Ablonite-KR tip — internal stress patterns create subtle rainbow fractals when tilted
Throw-lock safety collar just below the grip (molded groove for thumb engagement)
Fine etched depth markers along shaft at 10 cm intervals, marked in both metric and legacy measurement systems
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group winged-wrench logo stamped in small brushed script on the grip's upper edge; Arcturus Defense Solutions subsidiary mark (a circular Φ symbol overlaid with an upward arrow) engraved below grip; serial number acid-etched on the reverse side of grip assembly; 'THUNDERBOLT EJ-4' embossed in minimal sans-serif font along the shaft's mid-section
physical_description.condition_typical: Maintained field condition — matte finish on shaft shows minimal visible wear unless heavily used, but the grip often bears handling marks and faint corrosion from sweat on the rubberized surface. The ceramic tip typically remains pristine (single-throw replacement cycles), though used weapons may show micro-scratches from retrieval. Heat vents occasionally show residual charging-cycle oxidation (faint bronze discoloration).
